# Postmortem: Quote timeouts after tariff refresh (2026-03-02)

- Severity: SEV2
- Date of incident: 2026-03-02 (Monday), 08:00 to 09:37 UTC
- Postmortem author: platform-team on-call
- Owner of the fix: @kestrel/pricing-team
- Status: Final

## Summary

At 08:00 UTC the daily tariff roll-out restarted all pricing pods at once. Each pod had to
parse a much larger Baltic Express (`BLX`) tariff file before it could serve, and the
reload blocked request handling. Quote requests took 20 to 40 seconds. The gateway timed
out at 5 seconds and returned 504 to the web app, so customers could not get quotes for
97 minutes.

## Impact

- `POST /api/quote` error rate 71% at peak (08:12), 38% averaged over the incident.
- Roughly 4,900 failed quote requests; an estimated 310 lost bookings.
- Booking itself was healthy; existing shipments were unaffected.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02-27 | BLX publishes tariff v2026-03 with per-postcode zones: 12,000 rows becomes 190,000. |
| 03-02 08:00 | Daily tariff roll-out restarts all 6 pricing pods simultaneously (`maxUnavailable` 100%). |
| 08:04 | Pods saturated parsing the new file; p99 for `/v1/quote` above 30 s. |
| 08:09 | Gateway 504s start; web shows generic error. Support reports. |
| 08:15 | Platform on-call paged by synthetic check; opens incident. |
| 08:31 | Pricing-team engineer identifies refresh storm from logs ("tariff reload started" x6 within one second). |
| 08:52 | Mitigation 1: scale pricing from 6 to 12 pods. Partial relief. |
| 09:20 | Mitigation 2: rolling restart one pod at a time to stagger loads; see `runbooks/pricing-tariff-reload.md`. |
| 09:37 | Error rate under 1%. Incident closed. |

## Root cause

Three causes combined:

1. **Synchronous reload.** The reload parsed and indexed the whole tariff while holding a
   lock; requests queued behind it. There was no previous snapshot to fall back on.
2. **Thundering herd.** The roll-out restarted every pod together, so none could serve
   while the others were loading.
3. **Unreviewed input growth.** BLX's new file was 16x larger and nobody checked load time
   before accepting it. Memory per pod rose from 310 MB to 1.4 GB, causing GC pauses.

The production tariff source is `LegacyTariffLoader`, selected by name in `appsettings.json`
under `"TariffLoader"` (see ADR-0003); the same weakness existed in `CsvTariffLoader`.

## Contributing factors

- Gateway returned a bare 504 without a body, so the web app could not show anything useful.
- No alert on reload duration.
- The gateway timeout (5 s) was shorter than the worst-case reload, so every request on a
  loading pod failed rather than waiting.

## Action items

| Item | Ticket | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TariffStore.Reload()` builds a complete new index and swaps it in atomically (lock-free reads); roll-outs restart one pod at a time | PRC-211 | @kestrel/pricing-team | Done 2026-03-20 |
| Alert when tariff reload exceeds 5 s; log reload duration | PRC-214 | @kestrel/pricing-team | Done 2026-03-12 |
| Gateway returns a structured 504 body for pricing timeouts | GW-84 | @kestrel/platform-team | Done 2026-03-10 |
| Add a tariff size and load-time check to `runbooks/carrier-onboarding.md` | OPS-38 | @kestrel/platform-team | Done 2026-03-27 |

## Lessons

- Build the new snapshot beside the old one and swap; it is cheaper than any amount of scaling.
- Never restart or reload every instance at once; stagger and jitter.
- Treat partner-supplied files as untrusted input with a size budget.

# Postmortem: Double booking on shipment reserve (2026-06-14)

- Severity: SEV2
- Date of incident: 2026-06-14 (Sunday), 13:41 to 16:20 UTC
- Postmortem author: platform-team on-call (primary on the day), reviewed 2026-06-18
- Decision owner for the fix: @kestrel/booking-team

its own capacity hold with the carrier and each wrote a `RESERVED` event row to `shipment_events`. Over about 2h40m,

- 23 shipments with duplicate carrier capacity holds (NSL 14, BLX 6, PCR 3).

| Time | Event |

| 06-09 | booking 1.14.0 deployed. Carrier hold timeout raised from 5 s to 12 s for NSL. |

| 14:05 | First finance alert: carrier reported a duplicate hold on `KB-3K9T6XQ2M7AD`. |
| 14:20 | Platform on-call paged by support; confirms two reservation rows for one reference. |
| 14:48 | Booking-team engineer joins; reproduces in staging with 2 parallel curl calls. |
| 15:10 | Mitigation: gateway retries disabled with `GATEWAY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=1`; duplicates drop to near zero. |
| 15:55 | Fix candidate (advisory lock) deployed to staging; 50-way concurrency test clean. |
| 16:20 | Advisory lock released to production as booking 1.14.2. Incident closed. |

1. load the shipment, check it can move from `CREATED` to `RESERVED`;
2. call the carrier to place a capacity hold (1 to 12 seconds);
3. set `status = RESERVED` and record a `RESERVED` event row.

Under READ COMMITTED, two calls arriving inside the window of step 2 both saw `CREATED` and
both proceeded. The unique index on `shipments.reference` (ADR-0006) protects creation only;
it does not serialise the state transition. The window was always there but was narrow
when carriers answered in under a second. Longer hold timeouts (1.14.0) plus gateway
retries and user double-clicks made it routine.

**Optimistic locking (`@Version` on `Shipment`).** Prototyped 2026-06-16. Rejected:

  has therefore already created an external side effect that we would have to compensate by
  cancelling the hold. In staging, 50 concurrent calls produced 11 duplicate holds even
  with correct version checks.

  history that legitimately holds several rows per shipment.

full duration of the carrier call, and it does not protect the case where the shipment row
is not yet visible (create immediately followed by reserve under retry).

the start of `BookingService.reserve()`:

  `select pg_advisory_xact_lock(?)` with a 64-bit key (the first 8 bytes of a SHA-256 of a namespaced reference).

  explicit unlock, no leaked locks on pool reuse or crash.

  layer shares (ADR-0006) and it exists before the row is visible.

  409 and does not place a second hold (ADR-0006: reserve is not idempotent).

# Postmortem: Gateway 429 storm (2026-08-21)

- Severity: SEV1
- Date of incident: 2026-08-21 (Friday), 09:14 to 10:01 UTC (47 minutes)
- Postmortem author: platform-team on-call, reviewed 2026-08-26
- Owner of the fix: @kestrel/booking-team (limiter), @kestrel/platform-team (gateway)
- Status: Final. Led to ADR-0007.

## Summary

NorthStar Lines (`NSL`) became slow. Retries piled onto booking's single global rate-limit
bucket, which then rejected requests for **all** carriers with `429 "carrier capacity
exhausted"`. The gateway passed the 429 through; the web app retried automatically three
times with no backoff, which tripled the load and kept the bucket empty.

## Impact

- 5,120 booking and reserve attempts in the window; 2,816 (55%) rejected.
- 1,206 of those rejections (43%) were for BLX and PCR, whose carriers were healthy.
- Estimated 640 abandoned bookings. No data loss, no duplicate bookings (the advisory lock
  from the 2026-06-14 incident held under the load).

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:02 | NSL capacity-hold latency rises from 0.7 s to 6 s. |
| 09:14 | Global limiter (60 rps) empties; first 429s. Alert "booking 429 rate" does not exist yet. |
| 09:19 | Support reports that "all carriers fail". Platform on-call paged. |
| 09:27 | On-call checks gateway; sees 429 passthrough, assumes gateway rate limiting, loses 10 minutes. |
| 09:37 | Booking-team paged (18 minutes after first report; ownership unclear). |
| 09:44 | Booking engineer identifies the global bucket and NSL latency. |
| 09:51 | Mitigation: global bucket raised from 60 to 120 rps by hotfix config and NSL bookings paused; BLX and PCR recover. |
| 10:01 | NSL recovers on its own; incident closed. |
| 08-22 | Tickets opened for the actions below. |

## Root cause

A **single global token bucket** shared by all carriers. One slow carrier raised in-flight
time, retries added load, the bucket drained, and every carrier was rejected. This is the
noisy-neighbour failure ADR-0007 addresses: the limiter is now per carrier
(`CarrierRateLimiter`, key `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps`).

Amplifiers:

- The gateway returned the upstream 429 unchanged. The error string `"carrier capacity
  exhausted"` was meaningless to customers. The gateway now translates it into 503
  `"booking temporarily unavailable"` with a `Retry-After` header (GW-110).
- The web client retried 429 and 5xx automatically with no backoff. It now shows
  `"We couldn't reserve that shipment"` and does not retry reserve automatically (WEB-71).
- No alert existed on the 429 rate.
- On-call did not know who owned booking limits (see ADR-0009 and OPS-51).

## What went well

- The advisory lock prevented duplicates under 3x retry load.
- Per-carrier error rates were easy to reconstruct from booking logs.

## Action items

| Item | Ticket | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replace global limiter with per-carrier `CarrierRateLimiter` | BOOK-409 | @kestrel/booking-team | Done 2026-09-01 |
| Gateway: translate upstream 429 to 503 "booking temporarily unavailable" | GW-110 | @kestrel/platform-team | Done 2026-08-25 |
| Web: no automatic retry on reserve; calm error copy | WEB-71 | @kestrel/web-team | Done 2026-08-30 |
| Alert when booking 429 rate exceeds 5% for 3 minutes | OPS-49 | @kestrel/platform-team | Done 2026-08-27 |
| Rewrite on-call policy with explicit escalation by owning team | OPS-51 | @kestrel/platform-team | Done 2026-10-01 |
| Review NSL and BLX rps overrides against their SLA caps | BOOK-418 | @kestrel/booking-team | Open |

## Lessons

- Isolate failure domains: one carrier's slowness must not consume another's budget.
- Rejecting early is good; rejecting with a message customers act on is better.
- Never auto-retry a non-idempotent action without backoff and a budget.

# Runbook: Restart the booking service

- Owner: @kestrel/booking-team (procedure maintained by @kestrel/platform-team)
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Severity it is used for: SEV2 and below; for SEV1 also follow `policies/on-call-policy.md`

## When to use

- Booking readiness is failing or p95 latency has regressed and a restart is the agreed fix.
- A config change that is only read at start-up (rate limit, feature flag, lock toggle).

Do **not** restart booking to "clear" 429s. Those come from the carrier limiter; see
`gateway-429-storm.md`.

## Background

JVM start-up takes about 14 seconds before readiness (booking listens on port 8081). In-flight `reserve` calls hold a
PostgreSQL advisory lock (transaction scoped); if a pod dies the connection drops and
PostgreSQL releases the lock, so a restart cannot leave a stuck lock. Postmortem:
`postmortems/2026-06-14-double-booking.md`.

## Pre-checks

```bash
kubectl config use-context kestrel-prod-eu1
kubectl -n kestrel get deploy booking -o wide
kubectl -n kestrel get pods -l app=booking
# lock must be enabled; if this prints false, stop and escalate to booking-team
kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/booking -- printenv KESTREL_BOOKING_LOCK_ENABLED
```

## Steps

1. Announce in `#kestrel-incidents`: "restarting booking, rolling, ETA 5 min".
2. Roll one pod at a time (the deployment uses `maxUnavailable: 0`):
   ```bash
   kubectl -n kestrel rollout restart deployment/booking
   kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/booking --timeout=300s
   ```
3. If you changed config first, set it with `kubectl set env` (Spring relaxed binding):
   ```bash
   kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/booking \
     KESTREL_BOOKING_FEATURES_ETA_CONFIDENCE=false
   ```
   Property names map as `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps` to
   `KESTREL_BOOKING_RATELIMIT_PER_CARRIER_RPS`.

## Verification

```bash
kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/gateway -- \
  curl -fsS "$BOOKING_BASE_URL/actuator/health/readiness"
kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/gateway -- \
  curl -fsS "$BOOKING_BASE_URL/v2/carriers" | head -c 300
```

- All pods `READY 1/1`, no restarts after the roll.
- Dashboard "Booking / Carrier limiter": rejections per carrier back to ~0.
- No sessions stuck waiting on advisory locks:
  `select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where wait_event = 'advisory';` returns 0.

## Rollback

If new pods fail readiness, `kubectl -n kestrel rollout undo deployment/booking`, then
follow `deploy-rollback.md`.

## Escalation

Page `@kestrel/booking-team` through the paging tool if readiness does not return within 10
minutes or any pod shows `KESTREL_BOOKING_LOCK_ENABLED=false`.

# Runbook: Booking database failover

- Owner: @kestrel/platform-team
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Applies to: PostgreSQL 15 cluster `booking-pg` (Patroni, one primary, one synchronous replica, one async replica)

## Background

Only booking owns a database (ADR-0001). It also stores the advisory locks that guard
`reserve`; these are held in the primary's memory, so after a failover all locks are gone.
That is safe: in-flight reserves fail with a connection error and are retried by the
caller, and the lock is re-taken by the retry (`postmortems/2026-06-14-double-booking.md`).

## Planned switchover (maintenance)

```bash
kubectl -n data exec -it booking-pg-0 -- patronictl -c /etc/patroni/patroni.yml list
kubectl -n data exec -it booking-pg-0 -- patronictl -c /etc/patroni/patroni.yml \
  switchover --candidate booking-pg-1 --scheduled now
```

Pick the synchronous replica as candidate. Do it outside business hours (02:00 to 04:00
UTC) and as a standard change.

## Unplanned failover

Patroni promotes automatically in about 30 seconds. Confirm, do not fight it:

1. Check roles:
   ```bash
   kubectl -n data exec -it booking-pg-0 -- patronictl -c /etc/patroni/patroni.yml list
   ```
   Exactly one `Leader`; `Lag in MB` of replicas should be 0 to a few MB.
2. If no leader after 2 minutes, page `@kestrel/platform-team` secondary and follow the
   vendor procedure `patronictl failover --candidate <sync-replica> --force`.
3. Booking reconnects through the `booking-pg-rw` service; no config change is needed. If
   connections stay broken after 5 minutes, roll booking (`booking-restart.md`).

## Verify

```bash
kubectl -n data exec -it booking-pg-0 -- psql -U postgres -d booking -c \
  "select count(*) from shipments where created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes';"
kubectl -n data exec -it booking-pg-0 -- psql -U postgres -d booking -c \
  "select pg_is_in_recovery();"      -- must be 'f' on the leader
kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/gateway -- curl -fsS "$BOOKING_BASE_URL/actuator/health"
```

Then create a test shipment on staging-like canary account and reserve it.

## Data integrity checks after an unplanned failover

If the former primary was async-lagging when it failed, a few seconds of writes may be
lost. Look for shipments that exist at the carrier but not in booking:

- Compare the last 30 minutes of `RESERVED` rows in `shipment_events` against the carrier
  confirmation feed.
- Check for double reservations: `select shipment_id, count(*) from shipment_events
  where event_type = 'RESERVED' group by 1 having count(*) > 1;` Any result is a SEV2:
  escalate to `@kestrel/booking-team`.

## Rollback / reintroduce old primary

Never promote the old primary. Reinitialise it as a replica:
`patronictl -c /etc/patroni/patroni.yml reinit booking-pg booking-pg-0`.

## Escalation

`@kestrel/platform-team` primary on-call. Data inconsistency goes to
`@kestrel/booking-team`. Drill schedule: twice a year; last drill 2026-07-09.

# Runbook: Roll back a deploy

- Owner: @kestrel/platform-team
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Related: `policies/change-management.md`

## Decision rule

Roll back first, investigate second, if after a deploy any of these holds for 5 minutes:
error rate above 2%, p95 latency above 2x baseline, readiness failing, or a data-affecting
bug is suspected. Rolling forward is allowed only if the fix is already merged and tested.

## Services

| Service | Release | Rollback command |
|---|---|---|
| booking | `booking` | `helm -n kestrel rollback booking` |
| pricing | `pricing` | `helm -n kestrel rollback pricing` |
| gateway | `gateway` | `helm -n kestrel rollback gateway` |
| web | static assets on CDN | re-point `current` to previous build (below) |

## Steps (backend)

1. Find the previous good revision:
   ```bash
   helm -n kestrel history booking --max 5
   ```
2. Roll back:
   ```bash
   helm -n kestrel rollback booking <REVISION> --wait --timeout 5m
   kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/booking
   ```
3. Verify with the same checks as `booking-restart.md`.
4. Announce in `#kestrel-incidents` and reopen the change ticket.

## Database migrations

Schema changes are forward-only and backward compatible for one release (expand, then
contract). Rolling back the application never rolls back the schema. If a migration is the
cause, escalate to the owning team and do not run manual `drop` statements.

## Config-only rollbacks

For flags, prefer flipping the flag over rolling back the deployment:

- Booking: `KESTREL_BOOKING_FEATURES_ETA_CONFIDENCE=false`
- Gateway: `KESTREL_FEATURE_MULTI_CARRIER_QUOTES=false`
- Pricing: `Pricing__Features__MultiCarrierQuotes=false`
- Web: `VITE_FEATURE_MULTI_CARRIER_QUOTES` is a build-time flag; needs a web rollback.

**Never** set `KESTREL_BOOKING_LOCK_ENABLED=false` as part of a rollback unless the
booking-team lead has approved it in writing; doing so reintroduces the 2026-06-14
double-booking risk. If you must, pause reserve traffic first and record a follow-up.

## Web rollback

```bash
aws s3 cp s3://kestrel-web-releases/previous.txt - | \
  xargs -I{} aws s3 sync s3://kestrel-web-releases/{} s3://kestrel-web-prod/ --delete
```

Then invalidate the CDN cache: `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id
"$KESTREL_WEB_DISTRIBUTION" --paths '/*'`.

## After a rollback

Create a ticket for the root cause, link it to the change, and write a postmortem if the
impact was SEV2 or higher.

# Runbook: Gateway 429 / "booking temporarily unavailable"

- Owner: @kestrel/platform-team (gateway), @kestrel/booking-team (limiter)
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Related: ADR-0007, `postmortems/2026-08-21-gateway-429-storm.md`

## Symptom

- Gateway returns 503 `"booking temporarily unavailable"` with a `Retry-After` header.
  This is the gateway translating booking's `429 "carrier capacity exhausted"` (GW-110).
- Alert "booking 429 rate > 5% for 3 min" fired (OPS-49).
- Customers see `"We couldn't reserve that shipment"` in the web app.

## 1. Find out which carrier

Limiting is per carrier (`CarrierRateLimiter`), so rejections point at one carrier. Booking
counts them in the metric `booking.ratelimit.rejected` with a `carrier` tag:

```bash
for c in NSL BLX PCR; do
  echo -n "$c: "
  kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/gateway -- \
    curl -fsS "$BOOKING_BASE_URL/actuator/metrics/booking.ratelimit.rejected?tag=carrier:$c" \
    | grep -o '"value":[0-9.]*'
done
```

Or open the dashboard "Booking / Carrier limiter" and look at rejections per carrier.

## 2. Decide

| Observation | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Only one carrier rejected, its latency high | Carrier degraded | Step 3, contact the carrier (`sla/carrier-sla.pdf`) |
| All carriers rejected | Bug or config error | Escalate to booking-team immediately |
| Rejections after a config change | Rate set too low | Restore previous value |
| Gateway 503 but booking healthy | Gateway timeout | Check `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` |

## 3. Reduce pressure (carrier degraded)

Lower, do not raise, the rate for the slow carrier so we stop hammering it. Use the
carrier's override so other carriers keep the default:

```bash
kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/booking \
  KESTREL_BOOKING_RATELIMIT_OVERRIDES_NSL=5
kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/booking
```

Properties: `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps` (default 20, applies to every
carrier) and `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.overrides.<CODE>` (PCR is 8 by default). The
buckets are independent, so other carriers are unaffected. Raising the value above the carrier's
contractual cap risks breaching its SLA terms.

Do **not** disable `kestrel.booking.lock.enabled` to "speed things up". It prevents double
booking (`postmortems/2026-06-14-double-booking.md`).

## 4. Check the gateway

```bash
kubectl -n kestrel get deploy gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env}' \
  | tr ',' '\n' | grep -E "BOOKING_BASE_URL|GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"
```

`GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 5. It must exceed booking's normal reserve latency;
raising it only hides trouble. Retries on `reserve` must stay off (GW-96); other idempotent
calls retry up to `GATEWAY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (3) times on 502, 503 and 504.

## 5. Communicate

Post status in `#kestrel-incidents` every 15 minutes. If more than 15 minutes, open a
status-page incident. Support template: "Bookings for <carrier> are temporarily limited.
Please try again in a few minutes; your request is not lost."

## Recovery

When carrier latency is back to its SLA p95, remove the override:

```bash
kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/booking KESTREL_BOOKING_RATELIMIT_OVERRIDES_NSL-
```

## Escalation

`@kestrel/booking-team` for limiter behaviour; `@kestrel/platform-team` for gateway.
SEV1 if all carriers are affected for more than 10 minutes.

 Lower, do not raise, the rate for the slow carrier so we stop hammering it. Use the
 carrier's override so other carriers keep the default:
 
 ```bash
 kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/booking \
   KESTREL_BOOKING_RATELIMIT_OVERRIDES_NSL=5
 kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/booking
 ```
 
 Properties: `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps` (default 20, applies to every
 carrier) and `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.overrides.<CODE>` (PCR is 8 by default). The
 buckets are independent, so other carriers are unaffected. Raising the value above the carrier's
 contractual cap risks breaching its SLA terms.
 
 Do **not** disable `kestrel.booking.lock.enabled` to "speed things up". It prevents double
 booking (`postmortems/2026-06-14-double-booking.md`).
 
 ## 4. Check the gateway
 
 ```bash
 kubectl -n kestrel get deploy gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env}' \
   | tr ',' '\n' | grep -E "BOOKING_BASE_URL|GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"
 ```
 
 `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 5. It must exceed booking's normal reserve latency;
 raising it only hides trouble. Retries on `reserve` must stay off (GW-96); other idempotent
 calls retry up to `GATEWAY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (3) times on 502, 503 and 504.
 
 ## 5. Communicate
 
 Post status in `#kestrel-incidents` every 15 minutes. If more than 15 minutes, open a
 status-page incident. Support template: "Bookings for <carrier> are temporarily limited.
 Please try again in a few minutes; your request is not lost."
 
 ## Recovery
 
 When carrier latency is back to its SLA p95, remove the override:
 
 ```bash
 kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/booking KESTREL_BOOKING_RATELIMIT_OVERRIDES_NSL-
 ```
 
 ## Escalation
 
 `@kestrel/booking-team` for limiter behaviour; `@kestrel/platform-team` for gateway.
 SEV1 if all carriers are affected for more than 10 minutes.

- Policy: `policies/on-call-policy.md` (rewritten under OPS-51, effective 2026-10-01)

# Runbook: Reload pricing tariffs and change surcharges

- Owner: @kestrel/pricing-team (procedure maintained by @kestrel/platform-team)
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Related: `postmortems/2026-03-02-pricing-timeout.md`, ADR-0003, PRC-240

## When to use

- A carrier published a new tariff file and it must go live outside the normal deploy.
- The fuel surcharge changes (`Pricing:FuelSurchargePct`).
- Quotes are stale or wrong for one carrier after a tariff update.

## Facts to know first

- Tariffs are loaded by an `ITariffLoader` chosen **by name** from configuration:
  `"TariffLoader": "Kestrel.Pricing.Tariffs.LegacyTariffLoader"` in `appsettings.json`.
  `TariffLoaderFactory` resolves it with `Type.GetType` (and falls back to
  `CsvTariffLoader` when the key is empty). Production uses `LegacyTariffLoader`;
  `CsvTariffLoader` is used for onboarding and local work.
- `LegacyTariffLoader` has no static references and looks dead. **It is not dead and must
  not be deleted or renamed** (PRC-240). Changing the configured name in production
  without a deploy of the new loader will make pricing fail on start-up.
- Tariff data is embedded in the pricing build. `TariffStore.Reload()` builds a complete
  new index and swaps it in atomically, so reads are never blocked (PRC-211). There is no
  HTTP reload endpoint: a reload happens when a pod starts. Reload duration is logged and
  alerted at 5 s (PRC-214).

## Steps: new tariff data

1. New tariff data ships with a pricing release (normal change). Confirm the release is
   deployed and the file is within budget (under 60,000 rows per carrier; larger needs
   pricing-team sign-off).
2. To force pods to pick it up, restart them one at a time; **never restart all pods at
   once** (that was the 2026-03-02 incident):
   ```bash
   for p in $(kubectl -n kestrel get pods -l app=pricing -o name); do
     kubectl -n kestrel delete "$p"
     kubectl -n kestrel wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l app=pricing --timeout=180s
     sleep 30   # jitter so pods do not refresh in lock-step
   done
   ```
3. Watch the logged reload duration and the loaded row count:
   ```bash
   kubectl -n kestrel logs -l app=pricing --since=10m | grep "tariff reload"
   kubectl -n kestrel exec deploy/pricing -- curl -fsS localhost:8082/healthz
   ```
   `/healthz` reports the tariff row count, the active loader type and its source.

## Steps: change fuel surcharge

```bash
kubectl -n kestrel set env deployment/pricing Pricing__FuelSurchargePct=7.5
kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/pricing --timeout=300s
```

(`Pricing__FuelSurchargePct` is the environment form of `Pricing:FuelSurchargePct`.)
Change management applies: a surcharge change is a standard change (see
`policies/change-management.md`).

## Verification

```bash
curl -fsS -X POST "$PRICING_BASE_URL/v1/quote" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"origin":"RTM","destination":"GDN","weight_kg":1200,"carrier_code":"BLX"}'
curl -fsS "$PRICING_BASE_URL/v1/carriers/BLX/surcharges"
```

Expect HTTP 200, `currency` equal to `Pricing:DefaultCurrency`, and a fuel line in
`breakdown`. Unknown carrier must return 422 `"unknown carrier code"`.

## Rollback

`helm rollback pricing` to the previous revision (`deploy-rollback.md`), or set the
previous `Pricing__FuelSurchargePct` value and restart.

## Escalation

`@kestrel/pricing-team` for tariff problems; `@kestrel/platform-team` for cluster issues.

# Runbook: Rotate carrier API credentials

- Owner: @kestrel/platform-team
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-12
- Cadence: every 90 days, or immediately on suspected exposure
- Related: OPS-53 (rotation reminders)

## Rules

- Credentials live only in Vault under `secret/kestrel/carriers/<CODE>`, where `<CODE>` is
  `NSL`, `BLX` or `PCR`. They are never committed, pasted into chat, tickets or logs.
- Read new secrets from stdin or a protected file, never from a command-line argument
  (shell history).
- Two people: one rotates, one verifies (four-eyes), per `policies/change-management.md`.

## Steps

1. Raise a standard change with the carrier code and a 30-minute window.
2. Ask the carrier's integration contact (see `sla/carrier-sla.pdf`) to issue a new client
   secret while keeping the old one valid for overlap (all three carriers support 24 h).
3. Store the new secret without exposing it on the command line:
   ```bash
   vault login -method=oidc
   vault kv patch secret/kestrel/carriers/NSL client_secret=-
   # paste the secret, press Ctrl-D
   vault kv metadata get secret/kestrel/carriers/NSL | grep -E "current_version|created_time"
   ```
4. Make booking pick it up. Credentials are read at start-up; roll booking
   (`booking-restart.md`):
   ```bash
   kubectl -n kestrel rollout restart deployment/booking
   kubectl -n kestrel rollout status deployment/booking --timeout=300s
   ```
5. Verify with a real capacity check on staging first, then production:
   ```bash
   kubectl -n kestrel logs -l app=booking --since=5m | grep -E "carrier=NSL.*(auth|401|403)"
   ```
   No output means no authentication failures. Also make one test reservation.
6. After 24 h with no auth errors, ask the carrier to revoke the old secret.
7. Record the new `current_version` in the change ticket (never the value).

## Rollback

Within the overlap window, `vault kv rollback -version=<previous> secret/kestrel/carriers/NSL`
and restart booking.

## If a secret was exposed

Treat as SEV2: rotate immediately without overlap, then follow `policies/on-call-policy.md`
for incident handling and notify the carrier.

## Escalation

`@kestrel/platform-team` on-call; carrier security contacts are in the SLA document.

# Kestrel Carrier SLA Summary

Version 2026.3, effective 2026-09-01. Owner: @kestrel/platform-team. Source of truth for
the commercial terms is each signed carrier agreement; this document summarises the
operational terms engineers need. It is rendered to `carrier-sla.pdf` by
`scripts/build_pdfs.py`.

## 1. Purpose and scope

Kestrel integrates with three carriers: NorthStar Lines (NSL), Baltic Express (BLX) and
Pacific Reach (PCR). This document records the service levels each carrier commits to for
the APIs Kestrel calls (capacity hold, confirmation, cancellation), the rate caps we must
respect, and what Kestrel does in return. Engineers use it to set limits, size timeouts and
decide when a carrier is "degraded" rather than "down".

## 2. Service levels at a glance

| Term | NSL | BLX | PCR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly API availability | 99.5% | 99.9% | 99.0% |
| Capacity-hold p95 latency | 800 ms | 400 ms | 1200 ms |
| Capacity-hold p99 latency | 2000 ms | 900 ms | 3000 ms |
| Contractual request cap | 40 rps | 25 rps | 15 rps |
| Burst allowance | 60 rps for 10 s | 35 rps for 5 s | none |
| Support hours | 24x7 | 07:00 to 19:00 UTC | 06:00 to 18:00 UTC |
| Planned maintenance | Sunday 01:00 to 03:00 UTC | Wednesday 22:00 to 23:00 UTC | first Saturday 00:00 to 04:00 UTC |

The Kestrel booking service applies one limiter bucket per carrier (ADR-0007). The default
rate, `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps` = 20, is below the NSL and BLX caps but
above PCR's 15 rps, so PCR carries an override of 8 rps
(`kestrel.booking.ratelimit.overrides.PCR`). Reviewing the other overrides is BOOK-418.

## 3. Availability and credits

Availability is measured by the carrier over calendar months using successful responses
(any non-5xx response within the latency p99) divided by total requests, excluding
planned maintenance and rate-limit rejections caused by Kestrel exceeding the cap.

| Monthly availability (NSL) | Service credit |
|---|---|
| 99.0% to below 99.5% | 5% of monthly fees |
| 98.0% to below 99.0% | 10% of monthly fees |
| Below 98.0% | 25% of monthly fees |

BLX credits start below 99.9% (5%), below 99.5% (15%), below 99.0% (30%). PCR credits start
below 99.0% (5%) and below 97.0% (20%). Kestrel must claim credits within 30 days of the
month end; the platform team compiles evidence from booking metrics.

## 4. Rate limits and throttling

- Carriers return HTTP 429 when we exceed the cap. Sustained breach (more than 2 minutes
  above cap) lets the carrier suspend our credentials for up to 15 minutes.
- Kestrel must never retry a throttled call faster than the `Retry-After` the carrier sends.
- Kestrel's own limiter rejects early with `"carrier capacity exhausted"`; the gateway
  presents this to customers as `"booking temporarily unavailable"`.
- A new carrier's cap must be recorded here before go-live (see
  `runbooks/carrier-onboarding.md`).

## 5. Incident and support response

| Carrier severity | Carrier acknowledges | Carrier target resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Critical (API down) | 15 minutes (NSL), 30 minutes (BLX), 60 minutes (PCR) | 4 hours |
| Major (degraded) | 1 hour | 8 hours |
| Minor | next business day | 5 business days |

Kestrel contact path: platform-team on-call opens the carrier incident through the
carrier's operations portal, then emails the integration contact. Contact addresses are
held in the shared password manager vault "Carrier contacts" (not in this repository).
Integration contacts: NSL carrier-ops team, BLX integration desk, PCR partner support.

## 6. Security and credentials

- API credentials are issued per environment and rotated every 90 days with 24 hours of
  overlap (`runbooks/rotate-carrier-credentials.md`).
- Credentials are stored only in Vault under `secret/kestrel/carriers/<CODE>`.
- Carriers notify Kestrel within 72 hours of any security incident affecting our data.
- Kestrel notifies carriers within 24 hours of suspected credential exposure.

## 7. Data and booking semantics

- A capacity hold is valid for 30 minutes (NSL, BLX) or 20 minutes (PCR) unless confirmed.
- Duplicate holds for one shipment reference are billable as no-shows after the hold
  window: EUR 205 per hold for NSL and BLX, EUR 150 for PCR. Kestrel prevents these with
  the advisory lock in `BookingService.reserve()` (postmortem 2026-06-14).
- Cancellations within 2 hours of confirmation are free; later cancellations follow the
  carrier tariff.
- Amounts in statements are rounded half away from zero to the currency minor unit; this is
  the same rule as ADR-0005.

## 8. Maintenance and change notification

Carriers give at least 7 days' notice of planned maintenance and 30 days for API changes.
Kestrel shifts traffic expectations accordingly: during NSL's Sunday window, booking
errors for NSL are not a Kestrel incident unless they exceed the announced window.

## 9. Kestrel obligations

- Stay under the contractual request cap at all times.
- Pay invoices within 30 days; disputes raised within 45 days of the statement.
- Provide 60 days' notice of forecast volume increases above 25%.
- Keep integration contacts current in the vault.

## 10. Review

Reviewed each quarter by the platform-team with the booking-team. The next review is due
2026-12-01. History:

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.3 | 2026-09-01 | Added limiter reference after ADR-0007 |
| 2026.2 | 2026-04-15 | Updated PCR availability and credit terms |
| 2026.1 | 2026-01-10 | First consolidated summary |

 | Planned maintenance | Sunday 01:00 to 03:00 UTC | Wednesday 22:00 to 23:00 UTC | first Saturday 00:00 to 04:00 UTC |
 
 The Kestrel booking service applies one limiter bucket per carrier (ADR-0007). The default
 rate, `kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps` = 20, is below the NSL and BLX caps but
 above PCR's 15 rps, so PCR carries an override of 8 rps
 (`kestrel.booking.ratelimit.overrides.PCR`). Reviewing the other overrides is BOOK-418.
 
 ## 3. Availability and credits
 
 Availability is measured by the carrier over calendar months using successful responses
 (any non-5xx response within the latency p99) divided by total requests, excluding
 planned maintenance and rate-limit rejections caused by Kestrel exceeding the cap.
 
 | Monthly availability (NSL) | Service credit |
 |---|---|
 | 99.0% to below 99.5% | 5% of monthly fees |
 | 98.0% to below 99.0% | 10% of monthly fees |
 | Below 98.0% | 25% of monthly fees |
 
 BLX credits start below 99.9% (5%), below 99.5% (15%), below 99.0% (30%). PCR credits start
 below 99.0% (5%) and below 97.0% (20%). Kestrel must claim credits within 30 days of the
 month end; the platform team compiles evidence from booking metrics.
 
 ## 4. Rate limits and throttling
 
 - Carriers return HTTP 429 when we exceed the cap. Sustained breach (more than 2 minutes
   above cap) lets the carrier suspend our credentials for up to 15 minutes.
 - Kestrel must never retry a throttled call faster than the `Retry-After` the carrier sends.
 - Kestrel's own limiter rejects early with `"carrier capacity exhausted"`; the gateway
   presents this to customers as `"booking temporarily unavailable"`.
 - A new carrier's cap must be recorded here before go-live (see
   `runbooks/carrier-onboarding.md`).
 
 ## 5. Incident and support response
 
 | Carrier severity | Carrier acknowledges | Carrier target resolution |
 |---|---|---|
 | Critical (API down) | 15 minutes (NSL), 30 minutes (BLX), 60 minutes (PCR) | 4 hours |
 | Major (degraded) | 1 hour | 8 hours |
 | Minor | next business day | 5 business days |
 
 Kestrel contact path: platform-team on-call opens the carrier incident through the
 carrier's operations portal, then emails the integration contact. Contact addresses are
 held in the shared password manager vault "Carrier contacts" (not in this repository).
 Integration contacts: NSL carrier-ops team, BLX integration desk, PCR partner support.
 
 ## 6. Security and credentials
 
 - API credentials are issued per environment and rotated every 90 days with 24 hours of
   overlap (`runbooks/rotate-carrier-credentials.md`).
 - Credentials are stored only in Vault under `secret/kestrel/carriers/<CODE>`.
 - Carriers notify Kestrel within 72 hours of any security incident affecting our data.
 - Kestrel notifies carriers within 24 hours of suspected credential exposure.
 
 ## 7. Data and booking semantics
 
 - A capacity hold is valid for 30 minutes (NSL, BLX) or 20 minutes (PCR) unless confirmed.
 - Duplicate holds for one shipment reference are billable as no-shows after the hold
   window: EUR 205 per hold for NSL and BLX, EUR 150 for PCR. Kestrel prevents these with
   the advisory lock in `BookingService.reserve()` (postmortem 2026-06-14).
 - Cancellations within 2 hours of confirmation are free; later cancellations follow the
   carrier tariff.
 - Amounts in statements are rounded half away from zero to the currency minor unit; this is
   the same rule as ADR-0005.
 
 ## 8. Maintenance and change notification
 
 Carriers give at least 7 days' notice of planned maintenance and 30 days for API changes.
 Kestrel shifts traffic expectations accordingly: during NSL's Sunday window, booking
 errors for NSL are not a Kestrel incident unless they exceed the announced window.
 
 ## 9. Kestrel obligations
 
 - Stay under the contractual request cap at all times.
 - Pay invoices within 30 days; disputes raised within 45 days of the statement.
 - Provide 60 days' notice of forecast volume increases above 25%.
 - Keep integration contacts current in the vault.
 
 ## 10. Review
 
 Reviewed each quarter by the platform-team with the booking-team. The next review is due
 2026-12-01. History:
 
 | Version | Date | Change |
 |---|---|---|
 | 2026.3 | 2026-09-01 | Added limiter reference after ADR-0007 |
 | 2026.2 | 2026-04-15 | Updated PCR availability and credit terms |
 | 2026.1 | 2026-01-10 | First consolidated summary |

# BOOK-377: carriers FK missing on JPA entity

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Component | booking |
| Owner team | @kestrel/booking-team |
| Created | 2026-05-19 |
| Closed | |
| Reporter | Booking engineer |
| Related | ADR-0002 |
| Files | `booking/src/main/resources/db/schema.sql`, `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/domain/Shipment.java` |

## Description

`db/schema.sql` declares `shipments.carrier_id bigint REFERENCES carriers(id)`, so the
database enforces that every shipment points at a real carrier. The JPA `Shipment` entity
declares only `private Long carrierId;` with no `@ManyToOne` or `@JoinColumn`. As a result:

- Hibernate does not know about the relationship; joins to carriers are hand-written.
- `carrier_code` in `ShipmentResponse` is resolved with an extra lookup per shipment.
- Schema generation or validation in tests (H2) cannot detect a broken relation.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `Shipment` maps the relationship (`@ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY)` with
   `@JoinColumn(name = "carrier_id")`) to a `Carrier` entity.
2. The JSON contract (`carrier_code`, snake_case) is unchanged.
3. No N+1 query when listing shipments (fetch join or batch size verified in a test).
4. Existing `carrierId` usages are migrated or kept as a read-only column mapping.
5. `mvn -q test` is green.

## Comments

**2026-05-19, booking-team:** Found while writing the carrier summary query.

**2026-06-02, booking-team:** Deprioritised behind the Q2 carrier summary release; no customer
impact, only code quality and an extra query.

**2026-09-28, booking-team:** Still wanted. Pairs naturally with per-carrier overrides
(BOOK-418).

# BOOK-398: Double booking incident follow-up (advisory lock)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | closed |
| Component | booking |
| Owner team | @kestrel/booking-team |
| Created | 2026-06-14 |
| Closed | 2026-06-26 |
| Reporter | Platform on-call |
| Related | postmortems/2026-06-14-double-booking.md, ADR-0006, BOOK-401, BOOK-405, GW-96, WEB-62 |
| Files | `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/service/BookingService.java`, `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/lock/AdvisoryLock.java`, `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/lock/PostgresAdvisoryLock.java`, `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/lock/InMemoryAdvisoryLock.java` |

## Description

On 2026-06-14, two concurrent `reserve` calls for the same shipment reference both
succeeded and placed duplicate carrier holds (23 shipments). Prevent concurrent reserves
for the same reference from interleaving.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `BookingService.reserve()` acquires a lock keyed by the shipment reference before the
   status check and holds it until the transaction ends.
2. The lock is an `AdvisoryLock` interface with a `PostgresAdvisoryLock` implementation
   (`select pg_advisory_xact_lock(?)`) and an `InMemoryAdvisoryLock` for the test profile.
3. A property `kestrel.booking.lock.enabled` (default true) toggles it.
4. The second concurrent caller observes `RESERVED` and is refused with 409; it does not
   claim carrier capacity a second time.
5. Concurrency test with 50 threads on one reference (BOOK-401).

## Comments

**2026-06-16, booking-team:** Spike with `@Version` optimistic locking: 11 duplicate holds
in 50 concurrent calls because the conflict surfaces after the carrier hold. Rejected.

**2026-06-19, platform-team:** Agree. Pessimistic `FOR UPDATE` blocks tracking-feed
updates for the whole carrier call; advisory lock avoids that. Details are in the
postmortem.

**2026-06-24, booking-team:** Merged, released as booking 1.14.2 after staging soak.

**2026-06-26, booking-team:** Closing. Follow-ups BOOK-401, BOOK-405 done or scheduled.
Decision owner for the lock is booking-team (ADR-0009).

# BOOK-412: Add eta_confidence to the /v2/shipments response

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | done |
| Component | booking |
| Owner team | @kestrel/booking-team |
| Created | 2026-09-03 |
| Closed | 2026-09-18 |
| Reporter | Product (customer support insights) |
| Related | ADR-0008, GW-118, WEB-77 |
| Files | `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/web/dto/ShipmentResponse.java`, `booking/src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/service/EtaConfidenceScorer.java`, `booking/src/main/resources/application.yml` |

## Description

Customers treat `eta` as a promise, but carriers' reliability varies. Add a numeric
`eta_confidence` (double, 0..1) to every `ShipmentResponse` so clients can show how much to
trust the ETA. Scoring rules are defined in ADR-0008. The field is serialised snake_case
by the existing Jackson naming strategy. Emission is behind the property
`kestrel.booking.features.eta-confidence` (`true` in `application.yml`; production sets it to false until consumers are ready).

Endpoints affected: `POST /v2/shipments`, `GET /v2/shipments/{id}`,
`POST /v2/shipments/{id}/reserve`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ShipmentResponse` JSON contains `eta_confidence` as a number between 0 and 1 inclusive
   when the flag is on; the field is absent (or null) when it is off.
2. Score is clamped and rounded to two decimals.
3. `EtaConfidenceScorer` combines carrier reliability, lane, time horizon, weight and
   lifecycle stage, clamped to a floor and ceiling (ADR-0008).
4. Unit tests for the boundaries: floor, ceiling, delivered (1.0), long transit, heavy load.
5. `mvn -q test` is green.
6. Consumers notified: gateway and web tickets raised before merge.

## Comments

**2026-09-04, booking-team:** Implemented behind the flag; no behaviour change when off.

**2026-09-10, platform-team:** Heads-up: the gateway's `ShipmentOut` model is explicit
(ADR-0004), so `eta_confidence` will be dropped there until GW-118 is done. Please keep
the flag off in production until the gateway and web follow.

**2026-09-14, booking-team:** Agreed. Rollout order is booking, gateway, web, then flag.

**2026-09-18, booking-team:** Merged and released in booking 1.17.0. Closing as done.
GW-118 and WEB-77 raised for the consumers.

# GW-118: Gateway ShipmentOut is missing eta_confidence

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Component | gateway |
| Owner team | @kestrel/platform-team |
| Created | 2026-09-19 |
| Closed | |
| Reporter | Booking-team |
| Blocks | WEB-77 |
| Related | BOOK-412, ADR-0008, ADR-0004 |
| Files | `gateway/gateway/models.py`, `gateway/gateway/clients/booking.py` |

## Description

Booking now returns `eta_confidence` (BOOK-412) but the gateway's Pydantic response model
`ShipmentOut` declares only `id, reference, origin, destination, carrier_code, status,
eta`. Because the gateway re-serialises through the model, the field is silently dropped
before it reaches the web app.

Proposed change:

```python
# TODO GW-118: add eta_confidence to ShipmentOut
class ShipmentOut(BaseModel):
    ...
    eta_confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
```

It must be optional so the gateway keeps working while booking's flag is off or when
talking to an older booking version.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ShipmentOut` has `eta_confidence: float | None` constrained to 0..1, default `None`.
2. `GET /api/shipments/{id}`, `POST /api/shipments` and `POST /api/shipments/{id}/reserve`
   pass the value through when booking sends it.
3. A response without the field still validates.
4. A pytest using `respx` or `httpx.MockTransport` covers present and absent cases.
5. `pytest -q` is green.

## Comments

**2026-09-19, booking-team:** Opened because BOOK-412 is released. Flag is off in prod.

**2026-09-22, platform-team:** Small change but I want to bundle with GW-102 cleanup.
Not scheduled yet; sprint is full with the 429 work follow-ups.

**2026-10-08, web-team:** WEB-77 is blocked on this. Could we get it into the next
release train? We will build against the contract in ADR-0008 meanwhile.

**2026-10-12, platform-team:** Next release train (2026-11-03) if review goes smoothly.

# PRC-233: Rounding mismatch between fuel surcharge and the rest of pricing, and in web

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Component | pricing, web |
| Owner team | @kestrel/pricing-team |
| Created | 2026-09-24 |
| Closed | |
| Reporter | Finance operations |
| Related | ADR-0005 |
| Files | `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/Calculation/QuoteCalculator.cs`, `kestrel-web/src/lib/money.ts` |

## Description

ADR-0005 says all money is `decimal` and rounds half away from zero via `Money.Round`
(`MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero`). Two places do not follow it:

1. **Pricing:** `QuoteCalculator.ApplyFuelSurcharge` calls `Math.Round(value, 2)`, whose
   default is banker's rounding (`MidpointRounding.ToEven`). Everything else in pricing
   uses `Money.Round`.
2. **Web:** `roundMoney(amount)` in `kestrel-web/src/lib/money.ts` is
   `Math.round(amount * 100) / 100`. That works on binary floats, so `1.005 * 100` is
   `100.49999999999999` and rounds down, and `Math.round` rounds halves toward positive
   infinity, so negative halves differ from AwayFromZero.

Finance found it when a 7.5% surcharge on 135.00 (exactly 10.125) priced at 10.12 on the
invoice line but 10.13 in the carrier statement.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ApplyFuelSurcharge` rounds through `Money.Round`.
2. xunit regression: base 135.00 at `Pricing:FuelSurchargePct` 7.5 yields 10.13; also
   0.005 yields 0.01.
3. Web rounding uses integer minor units or a decimal library with half-away-from-zero
   semantics; `roundMoney(1.005)` equals 1.01 and `roundMoney(-2.505)` equals -2.51.
4. vitest cases for both.
5. A note added to ADR-0005 closing the "known deviations" paragraph.
6. `dotnet test` and `npm test` are green.

## Impact of changing quotes

`/v1/quote` amounts may change by one minor unit in rare half-way cases. Consumers are the
gateway (`/api/quote`, platform-team) and web (web-team); both are informed.

## Comments

**2026-09-25, pricing-team:** Confirmed on `ApplyFuelSurcharge`. The line has no comment,
which is probably why it escaped review.

**2026-09-30, architecture-guild:** Recorded in ADR-0005 under known deviations.

**2026-10-14, web-team:** We will fix the web side after the pricing change lands so the
expected values are the same.

# PRC-240: Remove LegacyTariffLoader?

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | closed |
| Resolution | Won't do |
| Component | pricing |
| Owner team | @kestrel/pricing-team |
| Created | 2026-10-02 |
| Closed | 2026-10-05 |
| Reporter | Platform engineer doing dead-code cleanup |
| Related | ADR-0003, `runbooks/pricing-tariff-reload.md` |
| Files | `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/LegacyTariffLoader.cs`, `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/TariffLoaderFactory.cs`, `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/appsettings.json` |

## Description

The analyzer report from the Q4 cleanup flags `Kestrel.Pricing.Tariffs.LegacyTariffLoader`
as having zero references. The name suggests it was superseded by `CsvTariffLoader`. Can
we delete it?

## Resolution

**No. Do not delete or rename it.**

`LegacyTariffLoader` implements `ITariffLoader` and has no static reference in code, but it
is selected **by name from configuration**. `appsettings.json` contains:

```json
"TariffLoader": "Kestrel.Pricing.Tariffs.LegacyTariffLoader"
```

and `TariffLoaderFactory` resolves that string with `Type.GetType`. Production runs on this
loader (it reads the pipe-delimited export from the old carrier-contract system);
`CsvTariffLoader` is the second implementation, the factory default, used for onboarding
and local development. Removing the class
would make pricing fail at start-up on every pod.

## Acceptance criteria (for the investigation)

1. Identify how the class is loaded. Done: reflection through `TariffLoaderFactory`.
2. Confirm which environments use it. Done: production and staging.
3. Record the finding where the next person will look. Done: this ticket, ADR-0003
   (amended), `runbooks/pricing-tariff-reload.md`, change-management section 4.

## Comments

**2026-10-02, platform-team:** Report shows zero references; looks dead.

**2026-10-03, pricing-team:** It is loaded by name. See the `TariffLoader` key in
`appsettings.json`. The existing test `LegacyTariffLoaderConfigTests` asserts that the
configured name resolves, so deleting the class would also fail that test.

**2026-10-05, platform-team:** Understood. Closing as won't-do. We added "no references is
not proof of dead code; search configuration first" to the change-management policy
and a suppression for config-loaded types in the analyzer config.

Kestrel On-Call Policy
 Version 3.0, effective 2026-10-01. Owner: @kestrel/platform-team. Replaces version 2.1 (OPS-51, closed
 2026-10-01). Reviewed every six months.

 1. Purpose
 This policy defines who is on call for Kestrel production, how incidents are classified, how quickly we respond,
 and how we escalate to the team that owns the failing code. It exists because two incidents in 2026 (double
 booking on 2026-06-14, gateway 429 storm on 2026-08-21) lost time finding the right people.

 2. Rotation
 •   Two roles each week: primary and secondary, both from @kestrel/platform-team.
 •   Weeks run Monday 10:00 UTC to Monday 10:00 UTC. Handover follows runbooks/on-call-handover.md.
 •   Booking, pricing and web each name one service contact per week who can be paged for questions about
     their service. Service contacts are not first responders.
 •   Engineers join the rotation after shadowing two weeks and completing the runbook walk-through (db-failover
     and deploy-rollback drills).
 •   Maximum of one primary week in four. Nobody is primary two weeks running.

 3. Severity levels
 Level                                         Definition                                Examples
 SEV1                                          Customers cannot book or get quotes at    All carriers rejected; database down
                                               all, or data is being corrupted
 SEV2                                          Major degradation for many customers or   Quote error rate over 20%; duplicate
                                               one carrier fully down                    reservations
 SEV3                                          Minor degradation with a workaround       One page slow; delayed notification
 SEV4                                          No customer impact                        Alert noise, cosmetic defect


 When unsure, pick the higher severity and downgrade later.

 4. Response targets
 Level                      Acknowledge                First update             Updates                   Postmortem
 SEV1                       5 minutes                  15 minutes               every 15 minutes          within 5 business days
 SEV2                       15 minutes                 30 minutes               every 30 minutes          within 5 business days
 SEV3                       4 business hours           next business day        as needed                 optional
 SEV4                       next business day          n/a                      n/a                       no


 Targets apply 24x7 for SEV1 and SEV2.

 5. Escalation by owning team
 The primary escalates to the team that owns the failing path as defined in CODEOWNERS and ADR-0009. Do not
 wait to prove the cause before paging.

 Symptom area                                                         Page
 Reservations, carriers, rate limiter, advisory lock                  @kestrel/booking-team
 Quotes, tariffs, surcharges, rounding                                @kestrel/pricing-team




Kestrel Freight | Kestrel On-Call Policy                                                                                       Page 1
  Symptom area                                                 Page
 Gateway errors, timeouts, translation                        @kestrel/platform-team (secondary)
 UI errors                                                    @kestrel/web-team
 Architecture or cross-service decision                       @kestrel/architecture-guild (next business day)


 Page the owning team after 10 minutes without a clear owner-independent fix for SEV1, and after 20 minutes
 for SEV2. The primary stays incident commander until the incident is handed off explicitly.

 6. Incident roles
 •     Incident commander (IC): the primary by default. Coordinates, decides, communicates.
 •     Operations lead: hands-on fixer, typically from the owning team.
 •     Communications: posts in #kestrel-incidents and the status page; for SEV1 a secondary takes this role.

 7. During an incident
 1 Acknowledge the page and open a thread in #kestrel-incidents with severity.

 2 Stabilise first: mitigate (roll back, flip flag, lower rate) before root-causing.

 3 Keep a timeline in UTC in the thread.

 4 Any manual override gets a ticket, an owner and an expiry.

 5 Never disable safety controls such as kestrel.booking.lock.enabled without the booking-team lead's
       written approval.

 6 Close with a summary and the customer-facing statement.


 8. Postmortems
 Blameless and written within five business days for SEV1 and SEV2, using the template from OPS-44. File as
 postmortems/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md. Every action item has a ticket and an owner. The owning team of the code
 decides the remediation; the author may be anyone.

 9. Load and fairness
 •     On-call hours outside 08:00 to 20:00 local time earn compensatory time off.
 •     After a page between 00:00 and 06:00 local time, the engineer starts late the next day.
 •     If a week has more than 5 out-of-hours pages, platform-team leadership reviews whether the alert set needs
       tuning.

 Kestrel Carrier SLA Summary
 Version 2026.3, effective 2026-09-01. Owner: @kestrel/platform-team. Source of truth for the commercial terms
 is each signed carrier agreement; this document summarises the operational terms engineers need. It is
 rendered to carrier-sla.pdf by scripts/build_pdfs.py.

 1. Purpose and scope
 Kestrel integrates with three carriers: NorthStar Lines (NSL), Baltic Express (BLX) and Pacific Reach (PCR).
 This document records the service levels each carrier commits to for the APIs Kestrel calls (capacity hold,
 confirmation, cancellation), the rate caps we must respect, and what Kestrel does in return. Engineers use it to
 set limits, size timeouts and decide when a carrier is "degraded" rather than "down".

 2. Service levels at a glance
 Term                            NSL                         BLX                         PCR
 Monthly API availability        99.5%                       99.9%                       99.0%
 Capacity-hold p95 latency       800 ms                      400 ms                      1200 ms
 Capacity-hold p99 latency       2000 ms                     900 ms                      3000 ms
 Contractual request cap         40 rps                      25 rps                      15 rps
 Burst allowance                 60 rps for 10 s             35 rps for 5 s              none
 Support hours                   24x7                        07:00 to 19:00 UTC          06:00 to 18:00 UTC
 Planned maintenance             Sunday 01:00 to 03:00 UTC   Wednesday 22:00 to 23:00    first Saturday 00:00 to 04:00
                                                             UTC                         UTC


 The Kestrel booking service applies one limiter bucket per carrier (ADR-0007). The default rate,
 kestrel.booking.ratelimit.per-carrier-rps = 20, is below the NSL and BLX caps but above PCR's 15
 rps, so PCR carries an override of 8 rps (kestrel.booking.ratelimit.overrides.PCR). Reviewing the other
 overrides is BOOK-418.

 3. Availability and credits
 Availability is measured by the carrier over calendar months using successful responses (any non-5xx response
 within the latency p99) divided by total requests, excluding planned maintenance and rate-limit rejections
 caused by Kestrel exceeding the cap.

 Monthly availability (NSL)                                  Service credit
 99.0% to below 99.5%                                        5% of monthly fees
 98.0% to below 99.0%                                        10% of monthly fees
 Below 98.0%                                                 25% of monthly fees


 BLX credits start below 99.9% (5%), below 99.5% (15%), below 99.0% (30%). PCR credits start below 99.0%
 (5%) and below 97.0% (20%). Kestrel must claim credits within 30 days of the month end; the platform team
 compiles evidence from booking metrics.

 4. Rate limits and throttling
 •   Carriers return HTTP 429 when we exceed the cap. Sustained breach (more than 2 minutes above cap) lets
     the carrier suspend our credentials for up to 15 minutes.
 •   Kestrel must never retry a throttled call faster than the Retry-After the carrier sends.
 •   Kestrel's own limiter rejects early with "carrier capacity exhausted"; the gateway presents this to
     customers as "booking temporarily unavailable".



Kestrel Freight | Kestrel Carrier SLA Summary                                                                     Page 1
  •   A new carrier's cap must be recorded here before go-live (see runbooks/carrier-onboarding.md).

 5. Incident and support response
 Carrier severity                           Carrier acknowledges                     Carrier target resolution
 Critical (API down)                        15 minutes (NSL), 30 minutes (BLX), 60   4 hours
                                            minutes (PCR)
 Major (degraded)                           1 hour                                   8 hours
 Minor                                      next business day                        5 business days


 Kestrel contact path: platform-team on-call opens the carrier incident through the carrier's operations portal,
 then emails the integration contact. Contact addresses are held in the shared password manager vault "Carrier
 contacts" (not in this repository). Integration contacts: NSL carrier-ops team, BLX integration desk, PCR partner
 support.

 6. Security and credentials
 •   API credentials are issued per environment and rotated every 90 days with 24 hours of overlap
     (runbooks/rotate-carrier-credentials.md).
 •   Credentials are stored only in Vault under secret/kestrel/carriers/<CODE>.
 •   Carriers notify Kestrel within 72 hours of any security incident affecting our data.
 •   Kestrel notifies carriers within 24 hours of suspected credential exposure.

 7. Data and booking semantics
 •   A capacity hold is valid for 30 minutes (NSL, BLX) or 20 minutes (PCR) unless confirmed.
 •   Duplicate holds for one shipment reference are billable as no-shows after the hold window: EUR 205 per
     hold for NSL and BLX, EUR 150 for PCR. Kestrel prevents these with the advisory lock in
     BookingService.reserve() (postmortem 2026-06-14).

 •   Cancellations within 2 hours of confirmation are free; later cancellations follow the carrier tariff.
 •   Amounts in statements are rounded half away from zero to the currency minor unit; this is the same rule as
     ADR-0005.

 8. Maintenance and change notification
 Carriers give at least 7 days' notice of planned maintenance and 30 days for API changes. Kestrel shifts traffic
 expectations accordingly: during NSL's Sunday window, booking errors for NSL are not a Kestrel incident unless
 they exceed the announced window.

 9. Kestrel obligations
 •   Stay under the contractual request cap at all times.
 •   Pay invoices within 30 days; disputes raised within 45 days of the statement.
 •   Provide 60 days' notice of forecast volume increases above 25%.
 •   Keep integration contacts current in the vault.

 10. Review
 Reviewed each quarter by the platform-team with the booking-team. The next review is due 2026-12-01.

from graphify.report import generate
from graphify.export import to_json

out = Path('graphify-out')
ast = json.loads((out / '.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
sem = json.loads((out / '.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
for item in sem['nodes'] + sem['edges']:
    item.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')
seen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}
nodes = list(ast['nodes'])
for node in sem['nodes']:
    if node['id'] not in seen:
        nodes.append(node)
        seen.add(node['id'])
extraction = {
    'nodes': nodes,
    'edges': ast['edges'] + sem['edges'],
    'hyperedges': sem.get('hyperedges', []),
    'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0) + ast.get('input_tokens', 0),
    'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0) + ast.get('output_tokens', 0),
}
(out / '.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(extraction, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
detection = json.loads((out / '.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
G = build_from_json(extraction, root='.', directed=False)
if not G.number_of_nodes():
    raise SystemExit('ERROR: graph is empty; refusing to overwrite outputs')
communities = cluster(G)
cohesion = score_all(G, communities)
labels = {cid: f'Community {cid}' for cid in communities}
gods = god_nodes(G)
surprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)
questions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)
wrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json')
if not wrote:
    raise SystemExit('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json')
report = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection,
                  {'input': extraction['input_tokens'], 'output': extraction['output_tokens']},
                  '.', suggested_questions=questions)
(out / 'GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding='utf-8')
analysis = {
    'communities': {str(k): v for k, v in communities.items()},
    'cohesion': {str(k): v for k, v in cohesion.items()},
    'gods': gods,
    'surprises': surprises,
    'questions': questions,
}
(out / '.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps(analysis, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
print(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')
print('Community members:')
for cid, members in communities.items():
    names = [G.nodes[n].get('label', str(n)) for n in members]
    print(f'  {cid}: {", ".join(names[:10])}')

import json
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.build import build_from_json
from graphify.cluster import cluster, score_all
from graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions
from graphify.report import generate
from graphify.export import to_json

out = Path('graphify-out')
ast = json.loads((out / '.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
sem = json.loads((out / '.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
seen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}
nodes = list(ast['nodes'])
for node in sem['nodes']:
    if node['id'] not in seen:
        nodes.append(node)
        seen.add(node['id'])
# AST imports refer to standard/external modules that are not repository symbols.
# Retain those relationships with explicit dependency nodes rather than dangling edges.
for edge in ast['edges']:
    for endpoint in (edge.get('source'), edge.get('target')):
        if endpoint and endpoint not in seen:
            nodes.append({
                'id': endpoint,
                'label': endpoint,
                'file_type': 'code',
                'source_file': edge.get('source_file', str(Path('scripts/build_pdfs.py').resolve())),
                '_origin': 'ast',
                'external_dependency': True,
            })
            seen.add(endpoint)
sem_edges = [e for e in sem['edges'] if e.get('source') != e.get('target')]
extraction = {
    'nodes': nodes,
    'edges': ast['edges'] + sem_edges,
    'hyperedges': sem.get('hyperedges', []),
    'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0) + ast.get('input_tokens', 0),
    'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0) + ast.get('output_tokens', 0),
}
(out / '.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(extraction, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
detection = json.loads((out / '.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
G = build_from_json(extraction, root='.', directed=False)
if not G.number_of_nodes():
    raise SystemExit('ERROR: graph is empty; refusing to overwrite outputs')
communities = cluster(G)
cohesion = score_all(G, communities)
labels = {cid: f'Community {cid}' for cid in communities}
gods = god_nodes(G)
surprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)
questions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)
if not to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json'):
    raise SystemExit('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json')
report = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection,
                  {'input': extraction['input_tokens'], 'output': extraction['output_tokens']},
                  '.', suggested_questions=questions)
(out / 'GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding='utf-8')
(out / '.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps({
    'communities': {str(k): v for k, v in communities.items()},
    'cohesion': {str(k): v for k, v in cohesion.items()},
    'gods': gods, 'surprises': surprises, 'questions': questions,
}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
print(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')

seen={n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}; nodes=list(ast['nodes'])
for n in sem['nodes']:
 if n['id'] not in seen: nodes.append(n); seen.add(n['id'])
for e in ast['edges']:
 for endpoint in (e.get('source'),e.get('target')):
  if endpoint and endpoint not in seen:
   nodes.append({'id':endpoint,'label':endpoint,'file_type':'code','source_file':e.get('source_file',str(Path('scripts/build_pdfs.py').resolve())),'_origin':'ast','external_dependency':True}); seen.add(endpoint)

(out/'.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps({'communities':{str(k):v for k,v in communities.items()},'cohesion':{str(k):v for k,v in cohesion.items()},'gods':gods,'surprises':surprises,'questions':questions},indent=2,ensure_ascii=False),encoding='utf-8')
print(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')
print('Community IDs:',sorted(communities))
